recipes.name: Apple Orchard Punch
ingredients_raw: 1 (32 fluid ounce) bottle apple juice, chilled
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen cranberry juice concentrate

steps.text: Combine apple juice, cranberry juice concentrate, and orange juice. Stir until dissolved; slowly add ginger ale.
Thinly slice apple horizontally. Float slices on top of punch.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Orchard Punch
raw_recipe.description: This apple orchard punch recipe is alcohol-free and combines apple, cranberry, and orange juices with ginger ale for a perfect drink for any occasion.

review.reviewBody: This was so delicious! It was definatley the hit of my Thanksgiving dinner, only wished I had doubled the recipe. I set aside some of the punch and froze it in ice cube trays to keep the punch cold longer, I added mandarin oranges to the cubes for decoration. FABULOUS

I like this punch very much and have made it for years. However, in the last say, 3-4 years I have been unable to find frozen cranberry juice anywhere. No stores around me carry it. I did find concentrated cranberry juice once, but it was unsweetened and the punch was awful. So, I figured out the proportions of the liquids and swapped the frozen cranberry for frozen apple juice (way easier to find) and used regular cranberry juice cocktail. I mean, it's basically just water taken out of one or the other to make concentrate, so I took the water out of the apple instead of the cranberry. I use 48 oz regular cranberry juice cocktail, 2/3 can of frozen apple, one cup orange juice and the 1.5 liter of ginger ale. To use a full can of frozen apple juice, everything else has to increase by 1.5. so that is 72 oz. (9 cups ) of cranberry, a whole 12 oz. can of froz. apple juice, 12 oz. (1.5 cups) orange juice and 2.25 liter (9.5 cups) of ginger ale. (If you just use the whole 2 liter bottle, you're only short 8 oz. of ginger ale, so the flavor isn't really too affected in that big of quantity.) You can also slice the frozen can in half and half the other stuff for a smaller quantity of punch. I usually do that and just make it twice if I run out (and I have that half can of frozen juice already waiting anyway.) I'm sure you could even quarter it if you only need a little...just keep the proportions the same. It would be nice if the recipe posted would show a substitution for the frozen cranberry juice since it is not so readily available.

I couldn’t find frozen cranberry juice concentrate, only cran-apple so I went to the local natural/organic market and got a bottle of unsweetened cranberry juice concentrate and added to taste, it was the perfect accompaniment with Thanksgiving dinner. This time, dinner was with non-drinkers so we used ginger ale but the next time...and there will be a next time...we’re going to use champagne. I highly recommend this recipe, it is perfectly balanced and quite festive!

Made this for a baby shower held in Dec. 2016. Was very well received by guests & Mom-to-be!! Used frozen apple juice & cranapple juice from the bottle and bottled oj. Didn't have gingerale, so used Sprite. Also put mandarin oranges & frozen cranberries to float in the punch. Was visually a lovely punch & was tasty, too. Several guests asked for recipe. Definitely a keeper.

I made this using a juice blend of cranberry and blackberry and blackberry ginger ale. To continue the theme, I added blackberries and orange slices with the apple slices. On the side of the punch bowl, I placed a bottle of spiced rum for those who wanted a spiked punch. Very good!
This was an unexpected hit at Thanksgiving! We made two batches, one as listed and one with Champagne instead of ginger ale for the adults. Yum!

This was a huge hit at our Thanksgiving dinner. We replaced the ginger ale with 2 bottles of Asti Spumante. For garnish, we floated a layer of fresh cranberries and placed orange slices on top. We served it in a drink dispenser on a wrought iron stand. It was beautiful as well as tasty!

I made this for my daughter and son-in-law's coed baby shower. It was a huge hit with both the men and women. Several people asked for the recipe. I would definitely make it again. I am so glad I made a double batch because it saved me from having to make a second one. The only thing different I did was I froze blueberries in apple juice small bowls to add to the punch as "ice."
I made this exactly according to recipe and it was ok...but when I poured 1 cup of punch into a half glass of reisling it made a really good sangria (also added frozen mandarin oranges).

This punch was a crowd pleaser. I made two different batches for the birthday party. The first one I made exact to recipe. the second batch I had "help" from my two year old and 2 l of ginger ale went in along with extra 12 oz of apple juice and the result was still excellent. I love forgiving recipes.

This was amazing! I couldn't find cranberry juice concentrate, so I used passion fruit juice concentrate instead. So delicious. Also, I doubled it, and used a full 4 liters of ginger ale. It was the only thing totally consumed by the end of the party!

Glad you brought this punch recipe back! I made it a number of years ago and lost the recipe. I made this for a baby shower and one of the aunts attending the went crazy for it. She used it for her Thanksgiving dinner that year. I love it because it is not sweet in the way many punch recipes can be. Using the thinly-sliced apples on top reinforce the harvest theme and adds a lovely look to the punch.
This punch was easy to make & delicious for the small wedding reception we had. I added frozen mixed berries for a nice decorative look & everyone enjoyed this punch!
Used cranberry-pineapple juice instead of cranberry concentrate. Loved it!

My daughter made this for a party we were having so there was a non-alcoholic punch. We didn’t add the ginger ale because not all the kids like carbonation. It was a hit and no one needed to add the ginger ale. (We had it next to the punch for people to add.)
Made this a few times now for different gatherings. Always a hit!

This is by far my favorite punch! I love the red color - perfect for the holidays and the flavors blend beautifully! I made it for a baby shower this past weekend with rave review from all in attendance.
My entire family truly enjoyed eating this dish and everyone rated it a "5." I will definitely make this dish again and again as this was mighty tasty and we cannot say enough about this dish.
I couldn't find cranberry concentrate. So I used extra cranberry juice to taste. Next time I'll measure! Great virgin and with champagne! A new favorite
